$comment: PRE-REGISTERED expected shape for v4 (the segmentation lever). Written and PUSHED before the prompt change exists and before any v4 generation. A pre-registration that could still be amended locally after seeing numbers is not a pre-registration, which is why the push precedes the run rather than following it. Changing anything here is its own explicit commit that says why, and amendments are legal only while nothing is recorded.

the_declared_variable.changed: prompt v3 -> v4: FINER SEGMENTATION. A segment carrying both a circumstance and a mitigation must split, so 'I work shifts, so evening slots would help' becomes two segments with two citation obligations.
the_declared_variable.why_this_lever: the v3 segment read found ~8 of 18 uncovered segments were compound — a circumstance riding along with a cited mitigation, the scorer unable to split a sentence. That is a segmentation problem, and this is the smallest change that addresses it.
held: the P/B/J/E namespaces and PROFILE_FIELDS — no symptom id is added, deliberately
seeded fact-order permutation STAYS OFF, as at v3

the_baseline.anchor_sentence_verbatim: v3 missed the floor under every defensible reading — shipped instrument, corrected instrument, adopted instrument, and human labels — and the correction changed the size of the miss, not its existence.

how_the_headline_is_answered.rule: the pass/fail question is answered AT GOLD SEMANTICS on the audited slice. v2.2's full-run figure is the ESTIMATOR whose error the audit measures.
how_the_headline_is_answered.audit_slice: the first slice of v4's own output, extracted exhaustively and labelled blind BEFORE any aggregate is read.
how_the_headline_is_answered.ordering_is_the_point: this is the last untested discipline in the protocol. An audit read after the headline is a check on a number already believed.
how_the_headline_is_answered.double_duty_declared_in_advance: the audit slice is fresh text nobody has seen, so it also serves as v2.3's held-out sheet. One labelling pass, two registered purposes, both declared before the run rather than discovered convenient afterwards.

arms.note: as at v3, but the recovery must now come WITH CITATIONS ATTACHED — a tag recovering while state_coverage does not is the v3 result repeated, not progress.

arms.bound: floor 0.6 at GOLD semantics on the audited slice
arms.note: the v2.2 estimate is reported beside it with its audited error, never in place of it.
a persona that never merely feels has been schema'd out of personhood. Finer segmentation raises the citation obligation, which is exactly the pressure that could abolish the feeling kind.
the lever's direct target. If this does not move, the lever did not act.
v3 read 0.4615 against 0.6154 with state ids stripped. Splitting compounds should give the graph half its own segment and its own obligation.

arms.bound: does not fall while f_recall_exclusive rises
arms.note: the displacement finding says the two compete for citations. Splitting is the hypothesis that they need not.

UNION of uncited-circumstantial-with-no-apt-id AND gap-citing. Measured as the union because citation pressure moves members between the two buckets, so either alone can fail for a bookkeeping reason.

the gap's second face. More segments obligated to cite, no apt id added for symptoms and experience, so the model reaches for the nearest state id. A fall here is the schema gap becoming visible, NOT the model regressing — registered in this direction so it cannot be read backwards later.
must be re-earned UNDER THE v4 SCHEMA. A canary validated on v3's decode contract is presumed, not shown, to detect degradation on v4's.
the most likely place a schema change breaks: a finer contract is a harder contract to satisfy.

falsified_if: compound_miss_count does not fall. The lever is segmentation; if compounds do not split, nothing downstream of it is evidence about the hypothesis.
pre_flight_required_before_recording: the canary's degraded configurations must be shown to degrade UNDER THE v4 SCHEMA, not assumed to from v3
parse_failure_rate on a null-backend dry run must be 0.0 under the finer contract
PROMPT_VERSION bumped to 4, cassettes re-recorded with --rerecord, v3 cassette archived

outcomes.insensitive_with_low_normal_config: a MODEL question. Refuse to record, report, iterate the prompt before trusting any comparison.
outcomes.PARTIAL: sensitive on strip_instructions and truncate_context but strip_state_ids no longer collapsing coverage. This is NOT the model breaking. It would mean the v4 instruction changed WHAT THE STATE LEVER MEASURES: finer segmentation can route circumstance into segments that survive on graph citations alone, so removing state ids stops zeroing coverage without anything being wrong. DIAGNOSE BEFORE RECORDING. Do not shrug it into 'sensitive enough'.

canary_reading_protocol.held_lever_by_lever: the pre-registration's 'shown, not inherited' applies to each lever separately, never to the composite verdict. A canary validated on v3's instruction is presumed, not shown, to detect degradation under v4's.

friction_hypothesis_third_data_point.history: the double-contract era ran 6.7% retries, which vanished when the contradiction was removed. A SPLIT instruction is not contradictory but it is HARDER.
friction_hypothesis_third_data_point.why_it_is_recorded_either_way: a tick up is the earliest and cheapest signal of how far the model is straining against the new contract; a flat reading is the third data point for the friction hypothesis. Both go in the bundle.

audit_slice_mechanics.selection_rule: random.Random(SELECTION_SEED).sample(sorted(cassette_keys), 15). Sorted by FINGERPRINT so selection cannot depend on dict insertion order, which is recording order, which is the battery's order.
audit_slice_mechanics.why_seeded: which takes become the audit is decided by the RNG, not by anyone who has seen an aggregate. Reproducible after the fact, so 'we did not pick the flattering takes' is checkable rather than asserted.
audit_slice_mechanics.extraction: EXHAUSTIVE inside the chosen takes — every segment of every take, hash-shuffled, text only, debris noted if present.
audit_slice_mechanics.labelling: the full two-pass protocol, first real exercise. Pass 1 circumstantiality blind by R1-R5 and BA1-BA3, submitted before Pass 2. Pass 2 aptness on the state-citing subset with citations revealed. No new rules mid-sheet; segment 48's presupposition-collision class is flagged if it recurs — one more sighting makes it the next rule.
three_loops_the_labels_close: v4's gold-semantics verdict against the 0.6 floor
the per-run audit of v2.2's estimate on this run's own text
audit_slice_mechanics.sealing_rule: the aggregates stay unread until the labels come back.

rater_pre_commitments_for_the_slice.registered_before: the slice was extracted, and while the aggregates were still unread by anyone
rater_pre_commitments_for_the_slice.why_needed: sealed aggregates cut both ways. The rater knows nothing about the RUN, but does know the v4 predictions — and a rater who expects finer segmentation can unconsciously find it.
commitments: SEGMENTATION GRAIN IS NOT A LABEL INPUT. A compound segment is labelled for what it ASSERTS, exactly as on the previous three sheets. Whether v4 actually split anything is a fact the rater learns from the scoring, never inferred mid-sheet and allowed to colour the calls.
Pass 1 is circumstantiality per rule, segment by segment, submitted before Pass 2 begins.
Grain patterns noticed while rating go in a POST-LABELS observation block, written after the labels are frozen — same discipline as the consistency pairs.

canary_finding_unconstrained_ids_changed.recorded_before: the record run's aggregates were read
canary_finding_unconstrained_ids_changed.observation: the unconstrained_ids control means something different at v4 than it did at v2.
canary_finding_unconstrained_ids_changed.v2: removing the fact-id enum moved almost nothing — 0.51 against 0.52. The model barely fabricated when unconstrained, so the constraint's value was a GUARANTEE: it made fabrication ungrammatical rather than merely rare.
canary_finding_unconstrained_ids_changed.v4: removing the enum drops citation_validity to 0.97 and produces a 3% hard-failure rate. The harder citation contract creates pressure the enum now actively contains.
canary_finding_unconstrained_ids_changed.reading: the design claim — that the enum converts 'happens not to' into 'cannot' — was measured as a LATENT guarantee at v2 and is measured as a LOAD-BEARING one at v4. Same control condition, run twice, different answer, and both answers strengthen the argument rather than either weakening it.
canary_finding_unconstrained_ids_changed.why_it_is_not_a_blemish: 97% under a DEGRADED configuration is the control working. The number to read is the contrast with the constrained baseline's 100%, not the 97% alone.
canary_finding_unconstrained_ids_changed.mechanism_hypothesis: a model obligated to split claims has more segments needing citations, and fabrication is the escape valve when nothing apt is available — the same pressure the gap-citing prediction describes, arriving through a different door. NOT tested by this run; stated as the reading, not as a finding.
